title: Three-Letter Long I
kidRule: The letters I, G and H work as a team of three to say the long I sound, and the G and H stay quiet! You usually find this team right before a T.
hint: I hear a long I sound here, and it is made by a team of three letters. Two of them stay quiet. Do you remember the team?
reminder: The long I sound here is spelled I-G-H, with a quiet G and a quiet H.

check.question: Why can't we hear the G and H in MIGHTY?
check.correctAnswer: I, G and H team up to say long I, so the G and H stay quiet!
distractors: Because the letter T makes every letter before it quiet
Because G and H are never heard in any word

words.sent: The mighty elephant pushed the log out of the road.
words.story: The mighty blue whale is the biggest animal that has ever lived. It is even bigger than the largest dinosaurs!
words.card: The *mighty* ant said she *might* carry the whole picnic home by herself!

words.def: On the night of this very day.
words.sent: We are having pancakes for dinner tonight.
words.story: On a clear, dark night far from city lights, you can see a few thousand stars with just your eyes!
words.card: *Tonight* an owl will deliver a *ton* of jellybeans to my window!

words.sent: Loud thunder can frighten my little dog.
words.story: A pufferfish gulps water and blows up like a spiky balloon to frighten away bigger fish!
words.card: Turn *right* at the pumpkin, but do not *frighten* the sleepy scarecrow!

words.def: To make something fit more closely or hold more firmly.
words.sent: Please tighten the lid so the juice does not spill.
words.story: Most screws and jar lids tighten when you turn them to the right. People remember it with the saying 'righty tighty, lefty loosey'!
words.card: It took *ten* octopuses to *tighten* the lid on the pickle jar!

words.sent: The baby squealed with delight at the bubbles.
words.story: Hundreds of years ago this word had no G or H in it. People added them later so it would match the word light!
words.card: The *deli* gave the dog a pickle, to his great *delight*!

words.sent: My left shoe is slightly bigger than my right one.
words.story: Your feet are slightly bigger in the evening than in the morning, because they swell a little as you walk around all day!
words.card: The feather was only *slightly* too *light* to win the arm-wrestling contest!

words.def: Standing straight up, not leaning or lying down.
words.sent: Meerkats stand upright to look for danger.
words.story: Penguins walk upright on two legs, just like people do, which is one reason they look as if they are wearing little suits!
words.card: The penguin stood *upright* and held *up* a sign that said 'Fish, please!'

words.def: The soft, dim glow in the sky just after the sun goes down.
words.sent: Fireflies began to blink in the twilight.
words.story: Animals that are most active at twilight, like rabbits and deer, have a special name: crepuscular!
words.card: At *twilight* the fireflies switch on every tiny *light* and play tag!

words.def: A bright flash of electricity in the sky during a storm.
words.sent: We saw lightning flash across the dark sky.
words.story: A bolt of lightning is about five times hotter than the surface of the sun!
words.card: The *lightning* was so bright that my flash*light* got jealous!

words.def: A small brown bird famous for its beautiful song, which it often sings after dark.
words.sent: A nightingale sang in the garden long after sunset.
words.story: A male nightingale knows hundreds of different tunes, and it is one of the few birds that sings in the middle of the night!
words.card: The *nightingale* sang all *night* until the moon asked for earplugs!
